For people who train

What Lou is using at Thrive in Bath

Thrive runs a working recovery clinic in Bath. Lou's sessions there are the same ones available to anyone who trains: hyperbaric oxygen in a hard-shell chamber you sit up in, and The Pod, which runs four recovery technologies in one session.

Hyperbaric oxygen

A pressurised, hard-shell chamber with windows and a reclining seat. You breathe oxygen through a mask for the session.

Red light

Red and near-infrared light, delivered in The Pod.

PEMF

Pulsed electromagnetic field, delivered in The Pod.

Hydrogen inhalation

Molecular hydrogen breathed during the Pod session.

Hydromassage

A water-jet massage bed, part of the same Pod session.

Book a session at Thrive Bath See clinic pricing

Thrive Bath is at The Foundry, Beehive Yard, Bath. Sessions are supplied for wellness and recovery use. If you are managing an injury or a medical condition, talk to your doctor or physio first and tell the clinic when you book.

How it helps

What a session does, in plain terms

Breathing oxygen at twice normal pressure dissolves far more of it into the blood than you can get at the surface, so it reaches tissue that is normally hard to supply. Done as a course of sessions, that is the dose the published research on performance and recovery is built on.

The most relevant trial for anyone who trains is a blinded, placebo-controlled study in trained athletes: after 40 sessions at 2.0 ATA they gained VO₂ max and raised their anaerobic threshold against placebo, with more mitochondria measured from muscle biopsy. In plain terms, the same effort sits further below the limit, without adding training load.

Hadanny et al., 2022, Sports Medicine - Open.

For academy owners and coaches

A chamber in your own academy

Academies already spend on mats, coaching and strength and conditioning. A hard-shell hyperbaric chamber puts recovery in the same building, so it happens between sessions rather than when someone gets round to it. These are the chambers used in the recovery rooms of professional sport, from a single seat to a four-person cabin.

Zeugma
1 person · the single-seat chamber most clinics and studios start with
Atlantis
2 people · shared sessions for a smaller facility
Mediterranean
4 people · group sessions for a squad or a busy academy
